metadata.title: OpenNWM: A Generalist Navigation World Model with Latent Action Pretraining
metadata.publication_status: Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027
metadata.note: The supplied manuscript does not identify authors or affiliations and does not state an accepted venue, DOI, arXiv URL, or publication year.

overview.tagline: Learn navigation dynamics from action-free video. Adapt them to physical actions.
overview.summary: OpenNWM learns a shared latent action interface from diverse navigation videos, uses it to pretrain a navigation world model, and adapts that model to real waypoint actions for prediction and planning.
overview.abstract: Navigation world models predict future observations conditioned on navigation actions to support planning, but their generalization across real-world environments remains constrained by the limited coverage of action-labeled data. Action-free navigation videos provide diverse visual experience, yet lack the recorded actions required for action-conditioned training. We introduce OpenNWM, a generalist navigation world model with latent action pretraining. It learns universal latent actions from large-scale action-free videos through visual prediction pretraining, and further aligns them with physical motions via action-conditioned post-training. To support video pretraining, we curate NavAnywhere, a large-scale action-free navigation video dataset comprising 17.5 million visual observations from 15 heterogeneous sources. It captures navigation by ground robots, humans, and drones, with diverse viewpoints and motion patterns across five broad scene types: residential areas, public and commercial spaces, urban settings, parks, and natural landscapes. Experiments demonstrate improved visual prediction on in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, together with improved navigation performance. These results show that latent-action pretraining enables diverse, action-free videos to improve dynamics learning and generalization for open-world navigation.

contributions.title: A shared latent action interface
contributions.text: Learn Universal Navigation Latent Actions through visual prediction, with physical motion supervision on annotated samples.

contributions.title: Action-free video pretraining
contributions.text: Pretrain navigation dynamics with inferred latent actions, then adapt the model to physical waypoint actions.

contributions.title: NavAnywhere
contributions.text: Bring together 17.5 million sampled observations from 15 sources spanning humans, ground robots, and drones.

contributions.title: Prediction and navigation evaluation
contributions.text: Evaluate direct visual prediction, autoregressive rollouts, LAM reconstruction, and navigation on in-domain and held-out datasets.

objectives.label: Visual prediction
objectives.description: Reconstruct the target observation from the current frame and inferred latent action.

objectives.label: Physical grounding
objectives.description: Predict physical motion from the latent action on motion-annotated trajectories.

objectives.label: Latent regularization
objectives.description: Regularize the latent posterior toward a standard normal prior.

lam.cache: Use the deterministic posterior mean from the 60K-step LAM checkpoint.

world_model.conditioning: Combine latent-action, temporal-horizon, and diffusion-timestep embeddings through adaptive layer normalization; attend to historical visual context through cross-attention.

stages.title: Latent-action pretraining
stages.conditioning: Inferred latent actions and relative time
stages.description: Learn navigation dynamics from action-free video using the LAM interface.

stages.title: Physical-action warmup
stages.description: Align a newly initialized physical-action encoder with the pretrained dynamics model.

stages.title: Joint post-training
stages.description: Jointly adapt physical action conditioning and visual dynamics.

nwm.conditioning_note: Relative time is always used; layer-normalized latent actions are used only for valid local offsets with absolute value at most 8.

ablation_differences.data: Smaller NavAnywhere subset for LAM training
ablation_differences.note: These settings belong to the ablation experiments, not the main reported training pipeline.

planning.summary: Optimize physical waypoint actions with the cross-entropy method, predict candidate futures, score them against the goal, execute the first action, and replan.
steps: Select elites and update the proposal
Execute the first action and replan
planning.note: Planning takes place in physical action space. The LAM auxiliary physical predictor is used for grounding during training, not for online planning.

navanywhere.name: NavAnywhere
navanywhere.statistics_note: Sequences are processed clips or trajectories; frames are sampled RGB observations; hours measure source-video duration. Action-annotated and held-out evaluation datasets are excluded.

sources.name: KrishnaCam

sources.name: Walking Tours
sources.description: Long-form internet walking tours and outdoor exploration.

sources.name: SANPO
sources.description: Real and synthetic egocentric navigation on sidewalks, roads, parks, and outdoor paths.

sources.name: CityWalker
sources.description: Urban sidewalks, intersections, pedestrians, and vehicles.

sources.name: The Great Outdoors

sources.name: i2Nav-Robot
sources.description: Campus buildings, streets, parking areas, and indoor-outdoor transitions.

sources.name: EgoWalk
sources.description: First-person walking in urban, residential, public, and recreational spaces.

sources.name: BotanicGarden
sources.description: Robot navigation among garden vegetation and pathways.

sources.name: In-house Collected

navanywhere.scene_note: Published percentages are rounded and sum to 100.1%.

sampling.note: EgoWalk is sampled from 100 Hz source video. Frame counts and source-video hours cannot be converted with one uniform frame rate.

navanywhere.rounding_note: The rounded source-hour rows sum to 1,188.64 h; the published total is 1,188.65 h. Scene percentages sum to 100.1% after rounding.

action_annotated.note: Go Stanford is held out for evaluation. TartanDrive is out of domain for the LAM and in domain for the post-trained NWM.

rows.name: TUM RGB-D
rows.description: Held-out RGB-D trajectories evaluated with supplied camera poses.

rows.name: Planetary Rover
rows.description: Lunar and Martian imagery from Chang’e-4 / Yutu-2 and Tianwen-1 / Zhurong with official pose metadata.

rows.name: Office-Go2
rows.description: In-house Unitree Go2 office recordings with synchronized camera poses.

direct_prediction.title: Direct visual prediction
direct_prediction.summary: OpenNWM leads all three ID aggregate metrics and PSNR on three of four OOD datasets. On Office-Go2, its PSNR is second, 0.036 dB below NWM†.

navigation.title: Navigation performance
navigation.summary: OpenNWM has the lowest reported ATE and best or tied-best RPE across RECON, SCAND, and Office-Go2.

lam_reconstruction.title: Latent action model reconstruction
lam_reconstruction.summary: The proposed LAM has the best reported PSNR and LPIPS in both ID and OOD reconstruction.

conditioning_ablation.title: Time and latent action conditioning
conditioning_ablation.summary: Combining time and latent action conditioning performs best on all six reported metrics in this ablation.
conditioning_ablation.evaluation_note: Direct LPIPS: Office-Go2 at 4 s. Autoregressive LPIPS: Go Stanford at 4 FPS up to 4 s. Lower is better for every metric.

lam_supervision_ablation.title: Visual and physical LAM supervision
lam_supervision_ablation.summary: Joint pixel and action supervision leads on five of six reported metrics; pixel-only has the lowest RECON RPE.
lam_supervision_ablation.evaluation_note: Direct LPIPS: Office-Go2 at 4 s. Autoregressive LPIPS: Go Stanford at 4 FPS up to 4 s. Lower is better for every metric.

semantic_consistency.title: Latent action semantic consistency
semantic_consistency.metric_definition: The unweighted mean recall over forward, backward, forward-left, forward-right, backward-left, and backward-right motions. Clusters and their majority motion labels are learned on in-domain data and transferred without reclustering.

scaling.title: Scaling action-free pretraining data
scaling.note: Four measured configurations with fixed labeled-data availability and the same fine-tuning protocol. Do not interpret interpolated values as experiments.
